build_note: Installed from the pinned pure-Python py3-none-any wheel and pinned dependency wheels by hash (pip --require-hashes, then pip check); the image checks that the wheel sqlfluff/ package is byte-identical to src/sqlfluff in the pinned sdist, that core/parser/lexer.py, dialects/dialect_ansi.py and the MIT LICENSE.md match recorded SHA-256 values, and that the optional sqlfluffrs Rust extra is absent, so the pure-Python lexer and grammar matcher run.
dependencies_note: Runtime dependencies pinned by hash: chardet 7.7.0, click 8.5.1, colorama 0.4.6, diff_cover 11.0.3 (with Pygments 2.21.0 and pluggy 1.7.0), Jinja2 3.1.6, MarkupSafe 3.0.4, pathspec 1.1.1, platformdirs 4.14.7, PyYAML 6.0.3, regex 2026.11.15, tblib 3.2.2 and tqdm 4.70.1. Parsing runs sqlfluff's own lexer and grammar; Jinja2 is reached only through sqlfluff's default templater, which passes this plain SQL through unchanged. The fuzz entry point is an external one-file Python bridge (linux/arm64 has no Atheris 3.1.0 cp314 wheel); the parser-line AFL++ bridge runs natively on arm64 to stay within afl-showmap's 30 s per-run limit.
parser_family: sqlfluff pure-Python lexer (core/parser/lexer.py) and dialect grammar matcher (core/parser/grammar, match_algorithms.py) over the ansi dialect segment definitions (dialects/dialect_ansi.py); independent of sqlparse, sqlglot, libpg_query and sqlparser-rs
api: sqlfluff.parse(local SQL text decoded from UTF-8 bytes, dialect="ansi") -> parse-tree record (nested {segment_type: value} mappings); the harness walks statement, select_statement, select_clause_element, join_clause, where_clause, groupby_clause, orderby_clause, function_name_identifier, table_reference, insert_statement, values_clause, quoted_literal and numeric_literal segments
fuzz_engine: external one-file Python bridge for AFL++ and generator replay
coverage: Python line tracing of the sqlfluff package source during valid-control replay; the AFL++ bridge maps the same traced lines
scope: One SQL statement from local text via sqlfluff.parse with the ansi dialect; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls only, each matching the hand-written oracle summary. Linting rules, fixing, other dialects, templaters beyond the default pass-through and the optional sqlfluffrs extra are untested.
